options.B: Purchasing stock in a target entity after overhearing an executive's discussion of a possible acquisition.
options.C: Deleting sensitive information from a final engagement communication at the request of senior management.
options.D: Investigating executive expense reports based completely on rumors of padding.

question: Which of the following statements is part of The IIA competency principle?

options.A: Internal auditors must disclose all material facts known to them that, if not disclosed, may distort the reporting of activities under review.
options.B: Internal auditors must respect and contribute to the legitimate and ethical objectives of the organization.
options.C: Internal auditors must be prudent in the use and protection of information acquired in the course of their duties.
options.D: Internal auditors must engage only in those services for which they have the necessary knowledge, skills, and experience.

question: When updating internal audit documentation containing sensitive data, which method best maintains confidentiality?

options.A: Using password-protected files on a shared drive with controlled access and routine backup procedures.
options.B: Storing all updated documentation in encrypted systems with access limited to authorized personnel and following data retention policies.
options.C: Saving updated documentation on a secure server with strict user authentication and periodic access reviews.
options.D: Maintaining documentation in an encrypted format on an internal portal with role-based access controls and audit trails.

question: Internal auditors specifically demonstrate conformance with the confidentiality principle by

options.A: Documenting distribution restrictions on engagement records.
options.B: Performing internal audit reviews in accordance with the Standards.
options.C: Obtaining new certifications and continuing professional education.
options.D: Disclosing all material facts to avoid distortion of reporting.

question: Internal auditors must apply due professional care in performing their work. They most likely apply due professional care by

options.A: Following the policies and procedures of the internal audit function.
options.B: All of the above.
options.C: Conforming with relevant codes of conduct.
options.D: Applying The IIA's mandatory internal auditing guidance.

question: Cosourcing of the activities of the internal audit function involves

options.A: Joint engagements with external service providers in order to mitigate self-review bias.
options.B: Performance of engagements by two or more external service providers in order to reduce audit costs.
options.C: External outsourcing of all the internal audit function's activities for one engagement due to in-house audit staff scheduling conflicts.
options.D: Ongoing outsourcing of internal audit function activities for IT and cybersecurity due to a lack of knowledge among in-house audit staff.

question: In an audit engagement involving the collection of customer data, which method best maintains confidentiality and proper use?

options.A: Collecting data via secure, encrypted channels and restricting access to only those explicitly authorized for the audit engagement.
options.B: Collecting data from approved sources and using internal software with default security settings to restrict access.
options.C: Acquiring data through standard methods and storing it in a shared drive with departmental access.
options.D: Obtaining customer data without formal encryption but limiting access through passwords.

question: A chief audit executive (CAE) has been requested by the audit committee to conduct an engagement at a chemical factory as soon as possible. The engagement will include reviews of health, safety, and environmental (HSE) management and processes. The CAE knows that the internal audit function does not possess the HSE knowledge necessary to conduct such an engagement. The CAE must

options.A: Defer the engagement and tell the audit committee that it will take several months to train internal audit staff for such an engagement.
options.B: Begin the engagement and incorporate HSE training into next year's planning to prepare for a follow-up engagement.
options.C: Seek permission from the audit committee to obtain appropriate support from an HSE professional.
options.D: Suggest to the audit committee that the factory's own HSE staff conduct the engagement.

question: An internal auditor is performing services in a division in which the chief financial officer is a close personal friend, and the internal auditor learns that the friend is to be replaced after a series of critical labor negotiations. The internal auditor relays this information to the friend. Has a violation of The IIA's Standards of Ethics and Professionalism occurred?

options.A: No. The use of the confidential information resulted in no personal gain to the internal auditor.
options.B: Yes. The internal auditor had a conflict of interest with the organization.
options.C: No. The internal auditor was just being honest with his or her friend.
options.D: Yes. The internal auditor was not prudent in the use of information acquired in the course of his or her duties.

question: An internal auditor judged an item to be immaterial when planning an assurance engagement. However, the assurance engagement may still include the item if it is subsequently determined that

options.A: Miscellaneous income is affected.
options.B: Related information is reliable.
options.C: Adverse effects related to the item are likely to occur.
options.D: Sufficient staff is available.

question: A manufacturing organization often hires recent college graduates to fill entry level internal auditor positions. Which of the following would not support the organization's commitment to the competency principle?

options.A: The organization routinely brings in motivational speakers to inspire the employees.
options.B: The organization pays for and requires all professional employees to take continuing education classes.
options.C: The organization requires a training program for entry level auditors.
options.D: Annually, the organization holds a seminar and provides the professional employees with updates on changes to IIA standards and guidance.

question: To comply with the confidentiality principle in The IlA's Standards of Ethics and Professionalism, internal auditors should

options.A: Use data encryption and restrict email distribution.
options.B: Not permit other auditors to issue false reports.
options.C: Omit observations from engagement reports.
options.D: Solicit feedback from internal audit stakeholders.

question: The internal audit function is considering hiring a person who has a thorough understanding of internal auditing techniques, accounting, and principles of management but has nonspecialized knowledge of economics and information technology. Hiring the person is most appropriate if

options.A: Other internal auditors possess sufficient knowledge of economics and information technology.
options.B: The prospective employee could reasonably be expected to gain sufficient knowledge of these competencies in the long run.
options.C: A mentor is assigned to ensure completion of an individually designed professional development program.
options.D: A professional development program is agreed to in advance of actual hiring.

question: Which of the following would violate The IIA's principle of competency?

options.A: The organization has downsized and has a very lean staff. The board has recently approved the deferral of all continuing education for the next 12 months due to the staff's workload.
options.B: The audit committee hired a new CAE to perform financial due diligence on a chain of hotels that the company is considering purchasing. The new CAE has extensive knowledge and years of experience in the hotel industry.
options.C: Carrie was recently promoted to supervise the audit of food and beverage accounting for the organization's banquet facilities. Carrie has audited several areas of the organization, including 6 months of shadowing audit supervisors in the hospitality area.
options.D: Bob recently completed continuing education courses in restaurant accounting and has been assigned to audit one of the organization's steakhouses next month.

question: When sharing audit findings with management, which method best ensures the confidentiality and appropriate use of sensitive information?

options.A: Using secure file transfer protocols and password-protected documents so that only authorized management receives the information.
options.B: Transmitting documents through internal messaging systems with standard security settings and limited access.
options.C: Sharing reports via a secure intranet portal with multi-factor authentication to verify recipient identity.
options.D: Distributing digital copies via secure email to management.

question: An internal auditor must write a summary report for senior management. How can effective written communication be applied to ensure the report is both informative and accessible?

options.A: By providing a broad overview with minimal focus on critical findings and recommendations.
options.B: By using formal language and long sentence structures to ensure clarity.
options.C: By including technical details and comprehensive background information for the reader.
options.D: By composing a concise summary that clearly states the objectives, key findings, and actionable recommendations in plain language.

question: Which of the following is a violation of The IIA's Standards of Ethics and Professionalism principle of confidentiality?

options.A: Confidential information of the organization was released in response to a court order received by the organization.
options.B: During an engagement, the audit supervisor found that a control deficiency caused by management override created exposure to material risks. He reported the matter to the audit committee.
options.C: A loan officer at the local bank requested financial statements for the past 2 years. The CFO approved the request.
options.D: Disclosure of the organization's trade secrets to a family member. The disclosure of the information resulted in no personal gain to the internal auditor or the family member.

question: Assurance engagements must be performed with proficiency and due professional care. Accordingly, the Standards require internal auditors to

options.A: Consider the probability of significant noncompliance, perform procedures so that all significant risks are identified, and weigh the cost of assurance against the benefits.
options.B: Consider the probability of significant noncompliance and weigh the cost of assurance against the benefits.
options.C: Perform procedures so that all significant risks are identified and weigh the cost of assurance against the benefits.
options.D: Consider the probability of significant noncompliance and perform procedures so that all significant risks are identified.

question: How should an internal auditor demonstrate professional skepticism when evaluating internal controls?

options.A: By assessing control evidence objectively, seeking additional validation, and questioning any discrepancies in the data.
options.B: By assuming that established controls remain effective based on their historical performance records.
options.C: By relying on standard procedures to review controls to detect any discrepancies.
options.D: By conducting routine checks and utilizing evidence provided.

question: During an audit engagement of operational processes involving proprietary information, how can an internal auditor ensure proper use of sensitive information?

options.A: By summarizing sensitive proprietary information in reports distributed to promote dissemination.
options.B: By transferring all collected proprietary information into a central database for ease of access.
options.C: By using secure audit software, following established data protection protocols, and sharing information only with authorized individuals.
options.D: By disseminating full details of proprietary data only in draft reports but not included in the final report.

question: Which of the following actions taken by a chief audit executive (CAE) could be considered professionally ethical under The IIA's Standards of Ethics and Professionalism?

options.A: To save organizational resources, the CAE limits procedures at foreign branches to confirmations from branch managers that no major personnel changes have occurred.
options.B: The CAE decides to delay an engagement at a branch so that his nephew, the branch manager, will have time to “clean things up.”
options.C: The CAE refuses to provide information about organizational operations to his father, who is a part owner.
options.D: To save organizational resources, the CAE cancels all staff training for the next 2 years on the basis that all staff are too new to benefit from training.

question: Due professional care calls for

options.A: Testing in sufficient detail to give absolute assurance that noncompliance does not exist.
options.B: Consideration of the possibility of material irregularities during every engagement.
options.C: Detailed reviews of all transactions related to a particular function.
options.D: Infallibility and extraordinary performance when the system of internal control is known to be weak.

question: In an assurance engagement of treasury operations, an internal auditor is required to consider which of the following?

options.A: Due to the recent sale of a division, the amount of cash and marketable securities managed by the treasury department has increased by 350%.
options.B: Both material and immaterial issues in regard to performance management.
options.C: The external auditors have indicated some difficulties in obtaining account confirmations.
options.D: The mix of investments is conservative and aligns with the organization's risk appetite.

question: An internal auditor judged an item to be material when planning an assurance engagement. However, the assurance engagement may exclude the item if it is subsequently determined that

options.A: Recurring income is involved.
options.B: Sufficient staff is not available.
options.C: Related information is unreliable.
options.D: Adverse effects related to the item are very unlikely to occur.

question: In an audit engagement that requires the review of third-party proprietary data, which practice best demonstrates respect for privacy and data ownership?

options.A: Obtaining third-party data without formal agreements, trusting that confidentiality will be maintained.
options.B: Accessing and using third-party data strictly under the terms of confidentiality agreements and secure transfer protocols.
options.C: Sharing third-party proprietary data with internal departments to obtain feedback from internal experts.
options.D: Distributing original third-party data within the organization to encourage feedback during the audit engagement.

question: The CAE is setting up a team to perform an assurance engagement on the organization's information system security structure. The organization has offices all over the world that rely on the system. The audit team will assess risks, monitor implementation of corrective action, and evaluate controls. Which of the following is an important question to answer when selecting the team to conduct this audit?

options.A: Are internal IT staff available to work on the internal audit engagement?
options.B: Are specialty skills from outside the internal audit department required?
options.C: Which auditors have the skills and experience required to implement recommended corrective actions?
options.D: How many hours are needed to complete the engagement?

question: Internal auditors should consider the relative complexity and extent of work needed when planning an internal audit engagement. This statement best aligns with which of the following principles?

options.A: Competence.
options.B: Objectivity.
options.C: Integrity.
options.D: Due professional care.

question: During digital communications in an audit engagement, which technique best safeguards sensitive information?

options.A: Using standard email services combined with secure file attachments and regular password updates.
options.B: Employing encrypted messaging applications and secure video conferencing with stringent access controls throughout the discussion.
options.C: Utilizing proprietary communication platforms with enhanced security features and monitored access logs during audit discussions.
options.D: Utilizing digital tools with periodic security checks with basic encryption features during discussions.

question: An internal auditor has some suspicion of, but no information about, potential misstatement of financial statements. The internal auditor fails to exercise due professional care by

options.A: Not testing for possible misstatement because the engagement work program had already been approved by engagement management.
options.B: Expanding the engagement work program, without the engagement client's approval, to address the highest ranked ways in which a misstatement may have occurred.
options.C: Identifying potential ways in which a misstatement could occur and ranking the items for investigation.
options.D: Informing the engagement manager of the suspicions and asking for advice on how to proceed.

question: Internal auditors' conformance with the competency principle most likely is demonstrated by

options.A: Retaining authorizations of all disclosures.
options.B: Documenting disclosures approved by legal counsel.
options.C: Prudence in using and protecting information.
options.D: Proper resourcing of engagements.

question: When collaborating with external stakeholders, how can an internal auditor ensure that confidential information is used appropriately?

options.A: By sharing summarized findings with external stakeholders while retaining full details for internal review only.
options.B: By consulting external experts on sensitive issues and later integrating their feedback into the audit report without further disclosure.
options.C: By disclosing only the necessary information under strict confidentiality agreements and in compliance with organizational policies and relevant laws.
options.D: By providing comprehensive details to external parties once a preliminary review is completed, ensuring transparency.

question: A small internal audit function is performing an assurance engagement but lacks the expertise to evaluate certain accounting estimates. Thus, the chief audit executive (CAE) must obtain the necessary knowledge, skills, and other competencies from an external service provider (ESP). The fundamental reason for this decision most likely is that

options.A: The CAE did not hire sufficiently qualified staff.
options.B: The quality assurance and improvement program (QAIP) failed to report the internal audit function's lack of expertise.
options.C: Each member of the internal audit function is not required to be qualified in all disciplines.
options.D: The ESP was needed to assume the role of CAE.

question: A staff internal auditor performed a portion of an engagement to review an organizational's marketing function. In particular, the internal auditor evaluated the function's effective and efficient use of resources to identify  1. Underused facilities  2. Overstaffing or understaffing  3. Nonproductive work  4. Procedures that were not cost justified To test for underused facilities, the internal auditor performed a complete walk-through of all spaces assigned to the marketing function and evaluated the use of both space and capital equipment. The internal auditor analyzed reports on space usage for the last year and concluded that facilities were neither underused nor used at maximum capacity. To test for overstaffing or understaffing, the internal auditor compared current staffing levels with a staffing analysis recently completed by an independent contractor. Because the staffing analysis used work standards and service demands to provide factual and reliable information on staffing requirements, the internal auditor was able to conclude that staffing levels were optimal. To test for nonproductive work, the internal auditor interviewed an employee from each level and, based upon their responses, concluded that no significant amount of nonproductive work was being performed. Thus, the internal auditor concluded that additional engagement work to search for procedures that were not cost-justified would not be necessary. In reference to requirements 1 and 2, due professional care...

options.A: Was not exercised because the internal auditor failed to apply reasonable care regarding requirement 2.
options.B: Was not exercised because the internal auditor failed to apply reasonable care regarding requirements 1 and 2.
options.C: Was exercised because the internal auditor applied reasonable care and competence in both areas.
options.D: Was not exercised because the internal auditor failed to apply reasonable care regarding requirement 1.

question: Due professional care implies reasonable care and competence, not infallibility or extraordinary performance. Thus, which of the following is unnecessary?

options.A: The reasonable assurance that compliance does exist.
options.B: 8. The conduct of extensive examinations.
options.C: The consideration of the possibility of material irregularities.
options.D: The conduct of examinations and verifications to a reasonable extent.

question: The IIA's Standards of Ethics and Professionalism apply to

options.A: A members but not candidates for certifications.
options.B: IIA members and certified internal auditors only.
options.C: Recipients of IIA certifications only.
options.D: All internal auditors.

question: Which of the following most likely constitutes a violation of The IIA's Standards of Ethics and Professionalism?

options.A: Auditor A accepted an assignment to perform an engagement at the electronics manufacturing division. Auditor A recently joined the internal audit function. But Auditor A was senior auditor for the external audit of that division and has audited many electronics organizations during the past 2 years.
options.B: Auditor C is content as an internal auditor and has come to look at it as a regular 9-to-5 job. Auditor C has not engaged in continuing professional education or other activities to improve effectiveness during the last 3 years. However, Auditor C feels performance of quality work is the same as before.
options.C: Auditor B has been assigned to perform an engagement at the warehousing function 6 months from now. Auditor B has no expertise in that area but accepted the assignment anyway. Auditor B has signed up for continuing professional education courses in warehousing that will be completed before the assignment begins.
options.D: Auditor D discovered an internal financial fraud during the year. The books were adjusted to properly reflect the loss associated with the fraud. Auditor D discussed the fraud with the external auditor when the external auditor reviewed workpapers detailing the incident.

question: A certified internal auditor performed an assurance engagement to review a department store's cash function. Which of the following actions will be deemed lacking in due professional care?

options.A: The final engagement communication included a well-supported recommendation for the reduction in staff, although it was known that such a reduction would adversely affect morale.
options.B: Organizational records were reviewed to determine whether all employees who handle cash receipts and disbursements were bonded.
options.C: Because of a highly developed system of internal control over the cash function, the final engagement communication assured senior management that no irregularities existed.
options.D: A flowchart of the entire cash function was developed, but only a sample of transactions was tested.

question: When internal auditors perform an assurance engagement, they consider

options.A: Whether the engagement needs to be supervised to ensure achievement of objectives.
options.B: The cost of assurance in relation to the potential benefits to be obtained.
options.C: Conformance with the organization's code of conduct rather than The IIA's Standards of Ethics and Professionalism.
options.D: How the assurance procedures can be certain to identify all significant risks.

question: In an internal audit engagement reviewing sensitive financial data, how can an auditor apply internal audit methodologies to maintain confidentiality and appropriate use of information?

options.A: By following secure data handling procedures, encrypting records, and limiting access to authorized personnel in accordance with organizational policies.
options.B: By relying on standard procedures and including a confidentiality clause.
options.C: By summarizing key findings in reports to avoid internal protocols for handling sensitive data.
options.D: By using the organization's standard data storage solutions.

question: A mid-sized company seeks to improve its internal audit reporting. How can effective written communication skills be applied to enhance audit reports?

options.A: By providing lengthy narrative explanations that cover all background information.
options.B: By emphasizing data presentation without summarizing the core insights for the intended audience.
options.C: By using clear, concise language with well-organized sections that highlight key findings and recommendations.
options.D: By incorporating specialized technical jargon and extensive details to demonstrate comprehensive expertise.

question: An internal auditor is preparing a written executive summary of an audit engagement. How should the auditor apply communication skills to ensure the summary is effective?

options.A: By providing a narrative that focuses on the audit methodology and avoids conclusions and recommendations.
options.B: By including technical details and data without other insights for executives.
options.C: By detailing every aspect of the audit process to ensure all information is covered.
options.D: By writing a succinct summary that presents audit objectives, key findings, and actionable recommendations in a straightforward manner.

question: How can an internal auditor maintain professional skepticism when facing potential bias during a self-review process?

options.A: By critically evaluating prior work with a fresh perspective and seeking external confirmation to offset inherent biases.
options.B: By reviewing previous work based on standard practices.
options.C: By relying on historical data and internal reviews to verify past work.
options.D: By comparing previous work with independent audit findings to identify signs of bias.

question: The IlA's due professional care standard applies to internal auditors' work.

options.A: States that they must consider the probability of any fraud.
options.B: Implies infallibility in certain matters.
options.C: Requires consideration of the materiality of the matters subject to an assurance engagement.
options.D: Implies that they are expected to give absolute assurance that noncompliance does not exist.

question: The internal audit function collectively must possess or obtain certain competency in

options.A: Contract law.
options.B: Marketing.
options.C: Information technology controls.
options.D: Management principles.

question: Company A recently acquired Company 8. Company B is in a very different industry from Company A. Ten internal auditors have been assigned to review key areas of Company B's operations. The CAE has arranged for the auditors to receive industry training prior to the commencement of work. How should the CAE explain to the board why the industry training is needed?

options.A: Internal auditors will not know how to be prudent in the use and protection of the information acquired in the course of their duties.
options.B: Internal auditors may distort the reporting of activities if all material facts are not known to them.
options.C: Internal auditors do not have the necessary knowledge, skills, or experience to complete the work.
options.D: Internal auditors will be unable to contribute to the legitimate and ethical objectives of the organization.

question: An organization has recently placed a former operating manager in the position of chief audit executive (CAE). The new CAE is not a member of The IIA and is not a CIA. Henceforth, the internal audit function will be run strictly by the CAE's standards, not The IIA's. All four staff internal auditors are members of The IIA, but they are not CIAs. According to The IIA's Standards of Ethics and Professionalism, what is the best course of action for the staff internal auditors?

options.A: They must resign their jobs to avoid improper activities.
options.B: The Standards do not apply because they are not CIAs.
options.C: They should comply with the Glo
options.D: They must respect the legitimate and ethical objectives of the organization and ignore the Standards.

question: The confidentiality principle in The IIA's Standards of Ethics and Professionalism is violated by

options.A: Failing to establish an active quality assurance program.
options.B: Participating in an activity that conflicts with the organization's interests.
options.C: Maintaining documentation of skills self-assessments.
options.D: Collecting data for internal use beyond that needed for the engagement.

question: Effective management of internal auditor objectivity most likely results from

options.A: Assignments based on familiarity with areas where auditors previously worked.
options.B: Determining that an area to be audited is acceptable given past experience.
options.C: Internal auditor self-assessments.
options.D: Training that reinforces professional skepticism.

question: When hiring entry-level internal auditing staff, which of the following will most likely predict the applicant's success as an internal auditor?

options.A: Level of detailed knowledge of the organization.
options.B: Ability to fit well socially into a group.
options.C: Ability to organize and express thoughts well.
options.D: Grade point average on college accounting courses.

question: To ensure that due professional care has been taken at all times during an engagement, the internal auditor should always

options.A: Communicate any noncompliance or irregularity discovered during an engagement promptly to the audit committee.
options.B: Consider the possibility of nonconformance or irregularities at all times during an engagement.
options.C: Ensure that all financial information related to the audit is included in the audit plan and examined for nonconformance or irregularities.
options.D: Ensure that all audit tests are fully documented.

question: Which of the following would not be permissible when outsourcing internal audit functions?

options.A: Cosourcing with external service providers for a specific engagement.
options.B: Outsourcing for the oversight of and responsibility for the internal audit function.
options.C: Outsourcing when internal auditors lack the knowledge or skills needed to perform all or part of the engagement.
options.D: Total external outsourcing on an ongoing basis where services are performed in accordance with the Standards.

question: Which of the following statements is true with regard to the external service providers?

options.A: An organization may outsource some, but not all, of the functions of the internal audit function to the external service providers.
options.B: An organization can engage external service providers associated with the engagement client to facilitate the completion of the engagement.
options.C: External service providers are used to determine whether the current staff is sufficient to satisfy the responsibilities of the internal audit function.
options.D: External service providers can provide the necessary knowledge, skills, and competencies to the internal audit function.

question: The internal audit function collectively must possess or obtain certain competencies. Internal audit staff should be competent in

options.A: Finance.
options.B: General management principles.
options.C: The use of the Glo
options.D: Marketing.

question: During a high-level meeting, an internal auditor must present key risk findings to senior leadership. How should the auditor apply ver

options.A: By reading the report to ensure no information is omitted.
options.B: By using a structured approach that emphasizes major risk points with clear explanations and relevant examples.
options.C: By giving background details with less emphasis on the core risk findings during the presentation.
options.D: By using technical terminology without simplifying concepts for nonspecialists.

question: An internal audit function has scheduled an engagement relating to a construction contract. One portion of this engagement will include comparing materials purchased with those specified in the engineering drawings. The internal audit function does not have anyone on staff with sufficient expertise to complete this procedure. The chief audit executive should

options.A: Delete the engagement from the schedule.
options.B: Perform the entire engagement using current staff.
options.C: Engage an engineering consultant to perform the comparison.
options.D: Accept the contractor's written representations.

question: The internal audit function collectively must possess or obtain certain competencies. Internal audit staff should be competent in

options.A: The exercise of business acumen.
options.B: Applying tax laws to returns.
options.C: Evaluating marketing campaigns.
options.D: Determining whether personnel decisions reflect general management principles.

question: When incorporating third-party data for audit evidence, which approach best applies internal audit methodologies to maintain confidentiality?

options.A: Using reliable third-party data as a primary source for audit evidence.
options.B: Obtaining data through secure channels and integrating it into the audit process in line with data protection policies.
options.C: Requesting third-party data through email.
options.D: Sharing all third-party data with the internal audit function to foster a collaborative review process.

question: Which principles of The IIA's Standards of Ethics and Professionalism require or recommend that internal auditors perform services in accordance with the Glo

options.A: Objectivity and confidentiality.
options.B: Competency and confidentiality.
options.C: Integrity and objectivity.
options.D: Integrity and competency.

question: During the course of an engagement, an internal auditor discovers that a clerk is embezzling funds from the organization. Although this is the first embezzlement ever encountered and the organization has a security department, the internal auditor decides to interrogate the suspect. If the internal auditor is violating The IIA's Standards of Ethics and Professionalism, the rule violated is most likely

options.A: Failing to exercise due diligence.
options.B: Lack of competence in this area.
options.C: Lack of loyalty to the organization.
options.D: Failing to comply with the law.

question: The board has asked the CAE to expand the scope of a current assurance engagement on organizational risk to evaluate the appropriateness of using self-insurance to minimize risk to the organization. Given the scope of the engagement requested by management, should the CAE consider engaging an actuarial consultant to assist in the engagement?

options.A: Yes. The actuary has skills not usually found among internal auditors to identify and quantify self-insurance risks.
options.B: Yes. An actuary is essential to determine whether the healthcare costs are reasonable.
options.C: No. It is a normal internal auditor function to assess risk; this engagement is therefore not unique.
options.D: No. The internal audit function is skilled in assessing controls, and the insurance control concepts are not distinctly different from other control concepts.

question: Internal auditors must apply the care and skill of a reasonably prudent and competent internal auditor. For example, in an assurance engagement, an internal auditor must

options.A: Perform assurance procedures that identify all significant risks.
options.B: Not consider cost when exercising due professional care.
options.C: Consider the use of technology-based analysis.
options.D: Communicate advice in accordance with the expectations of clients.

question: The CAE must ensure that the internal audit function is able to fulfill its responsibilities. Which of the following is an appropriate step to achieving this objective?

options.A: Identifying the available knowledge, skills, and competencies of the accounting department.
options.B: Identifying an internal auditor's education, previous experience, and specialized areas of knowledge during the hiring process.
options.C: Conducting periodic skills assessments to make sure each member of the internal audit function is qualified in all disciplines.
options.D: Ensuring that all internal auditors obtain experience in all aspects of the profession by not engaging external service providers.

question: The IIA's Standards of Ethics and Professionalism have five principles. Which principle addresses performance of work with diligence?

options.A: Confidentiality.
options.B: Due professional care.
options.C: Competency.
options.D: Objectivity.

question: In exercising due professional care, internal auditors must consider which of the following?

options.A: The extent of assurance procedures necessary to ensure that all significant risks will be identified.
options.B: The potential benefits of assurance procedures regardless of the cost of using the procedures.
options.C: The competence of the management team members who are colleagues of the CAE.
options.D: The relative complexity, materiality, or significance of matters to which assurance procedures are applied.

question: Internal auditing is unique in that its scope often encompasses all areas of an organization. Thus, it is not possible for each internal auditor to possess detailed competence in all areas that might be the subject of engagements. In which of the following must the internal audit function collectively be proficient?

options.A: Tax law.
options.B: Finance.
options.C: Emerging issues.
options.D: Commercial law.

question: An internal auditor observes that a new receivables clerk has access to accounting records. Accordingly, the auditor notes in the engagement working papers that controls over receipts are inadequate. Has the auditor exercised due professional care?

options.A: Yes, alertness to conditions most likely indicative of irregularities was shown.
options.B: Yes, irregularities were noted.
options.C: No, reasonable care was not taken.
options.D: Yes, the engagement working papers were annotated.

question: When the internal audit function outsources some of its functions to an external service provider (ESP),

options.A: Oversight of the internal audit function may be outsourced.
options.B: An ESP associated with the client is appropriate if the relevant guidance is followed.
options.C: The IIA's Standards must be followed by the ESP.
options.D: Responsibility for the internal audit function may be outsourced.

question: When incorporating confidential information into audit recommendations, which approach best ensures appropriate use?

options.B: Move the small tools inventory to the custody of the production inventory staging superintendent and implement the use of a special requisition to issue small tools.
options.C: Place supply of small tools in a secured area, install a key-access card system for all employees, and record each key-access transaction on a report for the production superintendent.
options.D: Close the exit to the employee parking lot and require all plant employees to use a doorway by the receiving dock that also provides access to the plant employees’ parking area.

question: Obsolete or scrap materials are charged to a predefined project number. The materials are segregated into specified bin locations and eventually transported to a public auction for sale. To reduce the risks associated with this process, an organization should employ which of the following procedures?

options.A: Permit employees to purchase obsolete or scrap materials prior to an auction.
options.B: Limit obsolete or scrap material to a pre-approved buyer.
options.C: Require managerial approval for materials to be declared scrap or obsolete.
options.D: Require that the auction house not be paid a commission.

question: Which of the following ensures that all inventory shipments are billed to customers?

options.A: Duties for recording sales transactions and maintaining customer account balances are separated.
options.B: Shipping documents are prenumbered and are independently accounted for and matched with sales invoices.
options.C: Sales invoices are prenumbered and are independently accounted for and traced to the sales journal.
options.D: Customer billing complaints are investigated by the controller's office.

question: Which of the following describes the most effective preventive control to ensure proper handling of cash receipt transactions?

options.A: Use predetermined totals (hash totals) of cash receipts to control posting routines.
options.B: Have bank reconciliations prepared by an employee not involved with cash collections and then have them reviewed by a supervisor.
options.C: One employee issues a prenumbered receipt for all cash collections; another employee reconciles the daily total of prenumbered receipts to the bank deposits.
options.D: The employee who receives customer mail receipts prepares the daily bank deposit, which is then deposited by another employee.

question: An internal auditor noted that several shipments were not billed. To prevent recurrence of such non-billing, the organization should

options.A: Undertake periodic tests of gross margin rates by product line and obtain explanations of significant departures from planned rates.
options.B: Release product for shipment only on the basis of credit approval by the credit manager or other authorized person.
options.C: Undertake a validity check with customers as to orders placed.
options.D: Numerically sequence and independently account for all controlling documents (such as packing slips and shipping orders) when sales journal entries are recorded.

question: The internal auditor recognizes that certain limitations are inherent in any system of internal controls. Which one of the following scenarios is the result of an inherent limitation of internal control?

options.A: The comptroller both makes and records cash deposits.
options.B: The organization sells to customers on account, without credit approval.
options.C: An employee who is unable to read is assigned custody of the organization's computer tape library and run manuals that are used during the third shift.
options.D: A security guard allows one of the warehouse employees to remove assets from the premises without authorization.

question: Which of the following controls would help prevent overpaying a vendor?

options.A: Reviewing and canceling supporting documents when a check is issued.
options.B: Reviewing the accounting distribution for the expenditure.
options.C: Requiring the check signer to mail the check directly to the vendor.
options.D: Approving the purchase before ordering from the vendor.

question: Which of the following activities performed by a payroll clerk is a contro! weakness rather than a control strength?

options.A: Draws the paychecks on a separate payroll checking account.
options.B: Prepares the payroll register.
options.C: Has custody of the check signature stamp machine.
options.D: Forwards the payroll register to the chief accountant for approval.

question: Organizational independence in the processing of payroll is achieved by segregation of functions that are built into the system. Which one of the following functional segregations is unnecessary for internal control purposes?

options.A: Segregation of payroll preparation and paycheck distribution.
options.B: Segregation of personnel function from payroll preparation.
options.C: Segregation of payroll preparation and maintenance of year-to-date records.
options.D: Segregation of timekeeping from payroll preparation.

context: Fact Pattern: The marketing department for a major retailer assigns separate product managers for each product line. Product managers are responsible for ordering products and determining retail pricing. Each product manager's purchasing budget is set by the marketing manager. Products are delivered to a central distribution center where goods are segregated for distribution to the company’s 52 department stores. Because receipts are recorded at the distribution center, the company does not maintain a receiving function at each store. Product managers are evaluated on a combination of sales and gross profit generated from their product lines. Many products are seasonal and individual store managers can require that seasonal products be removed to make space for the next season’s products.
question: Requests for purchases beyond those initially budgeted must be approved by the marketing manager. This procedure

options.A: Is a corrective control.
options.B: Is a detective control.
options.C: Is unnecessary because each product manager is evaluated on profit generated.
options.D: Should provide the most efficient allocation of scarce organizational resources.

context: A company employs three accounts payable clerks and one treasurer. Their responsibilities are as follows: Clerk 1 — Reviews vendor invoices for proper signature approval. Clerk 2 — Enters vendor invoices into the accounting system and verifies payment terms. Clerk 3 — Posts entered vendor invoices to the accounts payable ledger for payment and mails checks. Treasurer — Reviews the vendor invoices and signs each check.
question: A company employs three accounts payable clerks and one treasurer. Their responsibilities are as follows: Which of the following would indicate a weakness in the company's internal control?

options.A: Clerk 2 reconciles the accounts payable ledger with the general ledger monthly.
options.B: Clerk 3 mails the checks and remittances after they have been signed.
options.C: Clerk 1 opens all of the incoming mail.
options.D: The treasurer uses a stamp for signing checks.

question: An adequate system of internal controls is most likely to detect a fraud perpetrated by a

options.A: Single manager.
options.B: Single employee.
options.C: Group of employees in collusion.
options.D: Group of managers in collusion.

question: Organizational independence is required in the processing of customers’ orders in order to maintain an internal control structure. Which one of the following situations is a violation of the principle of the segregation of duties in the processing of orders from customers?

options.A: Invoice preparation by the billing department and posting to customers’ accounts by the accounts receivable department.
options.B: Approval by the sales department of a sales credit memo because of a product return with subsequent posting to the customer's account by the accounts receivable department.
options.C: Approval by credit department of a sales order prepared by the sales department.
options.D: Shipping of goods by the shipping department that have been retrieved from stock by the finished goods storeroom department.

question: A receiving department receives copies of purchase orders for use in identifying and recording inventory receipts. The purchase orders list the name of the vendor and the quantities of the materials ordered. A possible error that this system could allow is

options.A: Payment to unauthorized vendors.
options.B: Payment for unauthorized purchases.
options.C: Delay in recording purchases.
options.D: Overpayment for partial deliveries.

question: Which of the following would minimize defects in finished goods caused by poor quality raw materials?

options.A: Timely follow-up on all unfavorable usage variances.
options.B: Documented procedures for the proper handling of work-in-process inventory.
options.C: Determination of the amount of spoilage at the end of the manufacturing process.
options.D: Required material specifications for all purchases.

question: Ina well-designed internal control structure in which the cashier receives remittances from the mail room, the cashier should not

options.A: Endorse the checks.
options.B: Post the receipts to the accounts receivable subsidiary ledger cards.
options.C: Deposit remittances daily at a local bank.
options.D: Prepare the bank deposit slip.

question: The new controller of a company is evaluating her department for proper segregation of duties. Evaluate the following statements and determine which set of duties is acceptable to be performed by the same employee while still maintaining proper segregation of duties.

options.A: Authorize cash disbursements and deliver the payments.
options.B: Receive the company’s deposits and record the transaction.
options.C: Enter expenses into the general ledger and pay the credit card bills.
options.D: Collect the cash and checks and take the deposit to the bank.

question: How can segregation of duties best reduce fraud risk in inventory management?

options.A: Using an automated inventory system along with periodic inventory counts to control fraud risk.
options.B: Centralizing inventory management in one department and conducting inventory fluctuation trend analysis by another department to control fraud risk.
options.C: Assigning separate roles for inventory ordering, receiving, and recordkeeping to ensure independent performance of transactions.
options.D: Consolidating inventory ordering and receiving under one team and conducting periodic inventory counts to control fraud risk.

question: One control objective of the financing or treasury cycle is the proper authorization of transactions involving debt and equity instruments. Which of the following controls would best meet this objective?

options.A: Use of an underwriter in all cases of new issue of debt or equity instruments.
options.B: Segregation of responsibility for custody of funds from recording of the transaction.
options.C: Requiring two signatures on all checks of a material amount.
options.D: Written policies requiring review of major funding or repayment proposals by the board.

question: When reviewing an organization’s control structure, which aspect of authority levels most effectively helps prevent fraud?

options.A: Centralized authority concentrated in one individual, ensuring efficient oversight.
options.B: Clear segregation of authority that distributes decision-making power across multiple roles to create effective checks and balances.
options.C: Authority shared among several departments with ongoing control monitoring.
options.D: A hierarchical structure where authority is delegated to unrelated departments.

question: To minimize the risk that agents in the purchasing department will use their positions for personal gain, the organization should

options.A: Direct the purchasing department to maintain records on purchase prices paid, with review of such being required each 6 months.
options.B: Specify that all items purchased must pass value-per-unit-of-cost reviews.
options.C: Rotate purchasing agent assignments periodically.
options.D: Request internal auditors to confirm selected purchases and accounts payable.

question: An employee should not be able to visit the organization’s safe deposit box containing investment securities without being accompanied by another employee. What would be a possible consequence of an employee being able to visit the safe deposit box unaccompanied?

options.A: It would be impossible to obtain a fidelity bond on the employee.
options.B: The employee could pledge organizational investments as security for a short-term personal bank loan.
options.C: There would be no record of when organizational personnel visited the safe deposit box.
options.D: The employee could steal securities and the theft would never be discovered.

question: Reviewing an edit listing of payroll changes processed during each payroll cycle is most likely to detect

options.A: Inaccurate payroll deductions.
options.B: Labor hours charged to the wrong account in the cost reporting system.
options.C: Undetected errors in the payroll rates of new employees.
options.D: A failure to offer employees an opportunity to contribute to their pension plan.

question: An internal auditor noted that the accounts receivable department is separate from other accounting activities. Credit is approved by a separate credit department. Control accounts and subsidiary ledgers are balanced monthly. Similarly, accounts are aged monthly. The accounts receivable manager writes off delinquent accounts after 1 year, or sooner if a bankruptcy or other unusual circumstances are involved. Credit memoranda are prenumbered and must correlate with receiving reports. Which of the following areas could be viewed as an internal control weakness of the above organization?

options.A: Handling of credit memos.
options.B: Write-offs of delinquent accounts.
options.C: Monthly aging of receivables.
options.D: Credit approvals.

question: A utility with a large investment in repair vehicles would most likely implement which internal control to reduce the risk of vehicle theft or loss?

options.A: Physically inventory vehicles and reconcile the results with the accounting records.
options.B: Review insurance coverage for adequacy.
options.C: Systematically account for all repair work orders.
options.D: Maintain vehicles in a secured location with release and return subject to approval by a custodian.

question: Which of the following describes a control weakness?

options.A: Prenumbered blank purchase orders are secured within the purchasing department.
options.B: Purchasing procedures are well designed and are followed unless otherwise directed by the purchasing supervisor.
options.C: Normal operational purchases fall in the range from $500 to $1,000 with two signatures required for purchases over $1,000.
options.D: The purchasing agent invests in a publicly traded mutual fund that lists the stock of one of the organization's suppliers in its portfolio.

question: Which of the following controls could be used to detect bank deposits that are recorded but never made?

options.A: Having bank reconciliations performed by a third party.
options.B: Consolidating cash receiving points.
options.C: Establishing accountability for receipts at the earliest possible time.
options.D: Linking receipts to other internal accountabilities, for example, collections to either accounts receivable or sales.

question: One payroll engagement objective is to determine whether segregation of duties is proper. Which of the following activities is incompatible?

options.A: Hiring employees and authorizing changes in pay rates.
options.B: Signing and distributing payroll checks.
options.C: Preparing the payroll and filing payroll tax forms.
options.D: Preparing attendance data and preparing the payroll.

question: Control objectives regarding effectiveness and efficiency, reliability, and compliance are the basis of which control framework?

options.A: COBIT.
options.B: ITGI.
options.C: eSAC.
options.D: COSO.

question: When a supplier of office products is unable to fill an order completely, it marks the out-of-stock items as back ordered on the customer's order and enters these items in a back order file that management can view or print. Customers are becoming disgruntled with the supplier because it seems unable to keep track of and ship out-of-stock items as soon as they are available. The best approach for ensuring prompt delivery of out-of-stock items is to

options.A: Increase inventory levels to minimize the number of times that out-of-stock conditions occur.
options.B: Reconcile the sum of filled and back orders with the total of all orders placed daily.
options.C: Implement electronic data interchange with supply vendors to decrease the time to replenish inventory.
options.D: Match the back order file to goods received daily.

question: Which of the following internal control activities most likely would assure that all billed sales are correctly posted to the accounts receivable ledger?

options.A: Each shipment on credit is supported by a prenumbered sales invoice.
options.B: Each sales invoice is supported by a prenumbered shipping document.
options.C: Daily sales summaries are compared with daily postings to the accounts receivable ledger.
options.D: The accounts receivable ledger is reconciled daily to the control account in the general ledger.

question: An organization has computerized sales and cash receipts journals. The computer programs for these journals have been properly debugged. The internal auditor discovered that the total of the accounts receivable subsidiary accounts differs materially from the accounts receivable control account. This discrepancy could indicate

options.A: Credit memoranda being improperly recorded.
options.B: Receivables not being properly aged.
options.C: Statements being intercepted prior to mailing.
options.D: Receivables being lapped.

question: Which of the following is a factor in the control environment?

options.A: Information processing.
options.B: Performance reviews.
options.C: Management's philosophy and operating style.
options.D: Segregation of duties.

question: According to COSO, which of the following must be established prior to the risk assessment process?

options.A: Entity-level objectives.
options.B: Control activities.
options.C: External environment changes.
options.D: Fraud scenarios.

context: Fact Pattern: An organization has grown rapidly and has just automated its human resource system. The organization has developed a large database that tracks employees, employee benefits, payroll deductions, job classifications, ethnic code, age, insurance, medical protection, and other similar information. Management has asked the internal audit function to review the new system.
question: Human resources and payroll are separate departments. Which of the following combinations provides the best segregation of duties?

options.A: Payroll adds employees and enters employees’ bank account numbers but processes hours only as approved by human resources. Paychecks are automatically deposited in the employee's bank account.
options.B: Human resources adds employees, and payroll processes hours and enters employee bank account numbers. Paychecks are automatically deposited in the employee's bank account.
options.C: Human resources adds employees, payroll processes hours, and human resources delivers the paychecks to employees.
options.D: Human resources adds employees, reviews and submits payroll hours to payroll for processing, and delivers paychecks to employees.

question: Appropriate internal control for a multinational corporation's branch office that has a monetary transfer unit requires that

options.A: Foreign currency rates be computed separately by two different employees.
options.B: The branch manager receive all wire transfers.
options.C: Corporate management approve the hiring of monetary transfer unit employees.
options.D: The individual who initiates wire transfers not reconcile the bank statement.

context: Preliminary survey findings: (1) Department managers initiate purchase requests that must be approved by the plant superintendent. (2) Purchase orders are typed by the purchasing department using prenumbered and controlled forms. (3) Buyers regularly update the official vendor listing as new sources of supply become known. (4) Rush orders can be placed with a vendor by telephone but must be followed by a written purchase order before delivery can be accepted. (5) Vendor invoice payment requests must be accompanied by a purchase order and receiving report.
question: A preliminary survey of the purchasing function indicates that One possible fault of this system is that

options.A: Unnecessary supplies can be purchased by department managers.
options.B: Payment can be made for supplies not received.
options.C: Purchases could be made from a vendor controlled by a buyer at prices higher than normal.
options.D: Payment can be made for supplies received but not ordered by the purchasing department.

question: One characteristic of an effective internal control structure is the proper segregation of duties. The combination of responsibilities that would be consistent with the segregation of functional responsibilities is

options.A: Timekeeping and preparation of payroll journal entries.
options.B: Preparation of paychecks and check distribution.
options.C: Approval of time cards and preparation of paychecks.
options.D: Signing of paychecks and custody of blank payroll checks.

question: During an engagement involving a purchasing department, an internal auditor discovered that many purchases were made (at normal prices) from an office supplier whose owner was the brother of the director of purchasing. Controls were in place to restrict such purchases and no fraud appears to have been committed. In this case, the internal auditor should recommend

options.A: Establishment of a price policy (range) for all goods.
options.B: The development of an approved-vendor file initiated by the buyer and approved by the director of purchasing.
options.C: The initiation of a conflict-of-interest policy.
options.D: The inspection of all receipts by receiving inspectors.

question: An internal auditor is assigned to perform an engagement to evaluate the organization's insurance program, including the appropriateness of the approach to minimizing risks. The organization self-insures against large casualty losses and health benefits provided for all its employees. The organization is a large national firm with over 15,000 employees located in various parts of the country. It uses an outside claims processor to administer its healthcare program. The organization's medical costs have been rising by approximately 8% per year for the past 5 years, and management is concerned with controlling these costs. The healthcare processor wishes to implement controls that would help prevent fraud by dentists who are submitting billings for services not provided. Assume further that all the claims are submitted electronically to the healthcare processor. Which of the following control procedures would be the most effective?

options.A: Develop an integrated test facility and submit false claims to verify that the system is detecting such claims on a consistent basis.
options.B: Send confirmations to the dentists requesting them to confirm the exact nature of the claims submitted to the healthcare processor.
options.C: Require all submitted claims to be accompanied by a signed statement by the dentist testifying that the claimed procedures were performed.
options.D: Develop a program that identifies procedures performed on an individual in excess of expectations based on the age of the employee, whether a similar procedure was performed recently, or the average cost per claim.

context: Fact Pattern: An organization has grown rapidly and has just automated its human resource system. The organization has developed a large database that tracks employees, employee benefits, payroll deductions, job classifications, ethnic code, age, insurance, medical protection, and other similar information. Management has asked the internal audit function to review the new system.
question: An employee in the payroll department is contemplating a fraud involving the addition of a fictitious employee and the entry of fictitious hours worked. The paycheck would then be sent to the payroll employee's home address. The most effective control procedure to prevent this type of fraud is to require that

options.A: A report of all new employees added be approved by someone outside of the payroll department. Also, a report showing all employees and hours worked should be sent to the supervisor's department for review.
options.B: All changes to employee records be approved by supervisors outside of both human resources and payroll.
options.C: The payroll department physically delivers paychecks to employees rather than mailing them.
options.D: All new employees and their hours worked be entered by the human resources department.

question: During the preliminary survey for an audit of one of an organization's manufacturing plants, an auditor discovers that the plant experiences production problems with costs far in excess of those budgeted and with finished goods inventory levels that are clearly excessive. Which of the following management control procedures would have best brought the problems to management's attention earlier?

options.A: Planning monthly production based on management forecasts, with a report comparing actual production with forecasted production and actual costs with budgeted costs provided to management on a weekly basis.
options.B: Establishing perpetual inventory control procedures at each plant, with a report detailing any inventory items with levels in excess of two weeks’ production provided to management on a weekly basis.
options.C: Implementing standard costing procedures at each plant, with a summary of variances reported to management on a weekly basis.
options.D: Comparing actual sales with forecasted sales and budgeted gross margin with actual gross margin, with a report provided to management on a weekly basis.

question: Management's aggressive attitude toward financial reporting and its emphasis on meeting projected profit goals most likely would significantly influence an entity's control environment when

options.A: External policies established by parties outside the entity affect its accounting practices.
options.B: The audit committee is active in overseeing the entity's financial reporting policies.
options.C: Internal auditors have direct access to the board of directors and entity management.
options.D: Management is dominated by one individual who is also a shareholder.

question: Which of the following are included in the control environment described in the COSO internal control framework?

options.A: Organizational structure, management philosophy, and planning.
options.B: Integrity and ethical values, assignment of authority, and human resource policies.
options.C: Competence of personnel, backup facilities, laws, and regulations.
options.D: Risk assessment, assignment of responsibility, and human resource practices.

question: An internal auditor is assessing key risks in an organization's inventory management system. Which control is most effective in addressing the risk of stockouts?

options.A: Implementation of a perpetual inventory system.
options.B: Conducting semi-annual training for inventory staff.
options.C: Reordering based on historical sales data.
options.D: Regular inventory audits and reconciliations.

question: In financial reporting, which control best utilizes segregation of duties to enhance information reliability?

options.A: Implementing routine internal audit engagements of transactions while maintaining a centralized processing function.
options.B: Separating transaction authorization, recording, and reconciliation processes to provide independent checks at every stage.
options.C: Relying on an automated system to perform all transaction functions combined with reconciliation by the accounting department.
options.D: Combining authorization and recording functions and utilizing periodic supervisory reviews for validation.

question: During an engagement involving a construction contract, the internal auditor discovered that the contractor was being paid for each ton of dirt removed. The contract called for payment based on cubic yards removed. Which internal control might have prevented this error?

options.A: Comparison of invoices with purchase orders or contracts.
options.B: Extension checks of invoice amounts.
options.C: Comparison of invoices with receiving reports.
options.D: Comparison of actual costs with budgeted costs.

question: Management can best strengthen internal control over the custody of inventory stored in an off-site warehouse by implementing

options.A: Increases in insurance coverage.
options.B: Regular reconciliation of physical inventories to accounting records.
options.C: Reconciliations of transfer slips to/from the warehouse with inventory records.
options.D: Regular confirmation of the amount on hand with the custodian of the warehouse.

question: According to COSO, management oversight of the effectiveness of internal control provides evidence for which of the following control components?

options.A: Monitoring activities.
options.B: Risk assessment.
options.C: Information and communication.
options.D: Control activities.

question: Which of the following internal control activities most effectively helps prevent payroll fraud involving ghost employees?

options.A: Conducting surprise cash counts in the payroll department.
options.B: Comparing budgeted with actual payroll expenses quarterly.
options.C: Requiring two signatures on all outgoing checks.
options.D: Segregating the duties of payroll processing and payroll approval.

question: Which of the following controls would prevent the ordering of quantities in excess of an organization’s needs?

options.A: A policy requiring review of the purchase order before receiving a new shipment.
options.B: Automatic reorder by the purchasing department when low inventory level is indicated by the system.
options.C: A policy requiring agreement of the receiving report and packing slip before storage of new receipts.
options.D: Review of all purchase requisitions by a supervisor in the user department prior to submitting them to the purchasing department.

question: To minimize potential financial losses associated with physical assets, the assets should be insured in an amount that is

options.A: Equal to the book value of the individual assets.
options.B: Supported by periodic appraisals.
options.C: Determined by the board of directors.
options.D: Automatically adjusted by an economic indicator such as the consumer price index.

context: Fact Pattern: An organization has grown rapidly and has just automated its human resource system. The organization has developed a large database that tracks employees, employee benefits, payroll deductions, job classifications, ethnic code, age, insurance, medical protection, and other similar information. Management has asked the internal audit function to review the new system.
question: The automated system contains a table of pay rates matched with the employee job classifications. The best control to ensure that the table is updated correctly for only valid pay changes is to

options.A: Require that all pay changes be signed by the employee to verify that the change goes to a bona fide employee.
options.B: Ensure that adequate edit and reasonableness checks are built into the automated system.
options.C: Require a supervisor in the department, who does not have the ability to change the table of pay rates, to compare the changes with a signed management authorization.
options.D: Limit access to the data table to management and line supervisors who have the authority to determine pay rates.

question: Management is concerned with the potential for unauthorized changes in the payroll. Which of the following is the proper organizational structure to prevent such unauthorized changes?

options.A: The payroll department is supervised by the management of the human resources division.
options.B: The payroll department's functions are limited to maintaining the payroll records, distributing paychecks, and posting the payroll entries to the general ledger.
options.C: The personnel department authorizes the hiring and pay levels of all employees.
options.D: The payroll department maintains and authorizes all changes in the personnel records.

question: An internal control narrative indicates that an approved voucher is required to support every check request for payment of merchandise. Which of the following audit procedures provides the greatest assurance that this control is operating effectively?

options.A: Select and examine canceled checks and ascertain that the related vouchers are dated no earlier than the checks.
options.B: Select and examine vouchers and ascertain that the related canceled checks are dated no earlier than the vouchers.
options.C: Select and examine canceled checks and ascertain that the related vouchers are dated no later than the checks.
options.D: Select and examine vouchers and ascertain that the related canceled checks are dated no later than the vouchers.

question: Which of the following situations will cause an internal auditor to question the adequacy of controls over a purchasing function?

options.A: The original and one copy of the purchase order are mailed to the vendor. The copy on which the vendor acknowledges acceptance is returned to the purchasing department.
options.B: Receiving reports are forwarded to purchasing where they are matched with purchase orders and sent to accounts payable.
options.C: Unpaid voucher files and perpetual inventory records are independently maintained.
options.D: The accounts payable section prepares documentation for payments.

question: Which of the following activities represents both an appropriate human resources department function and a deterrent to payroll fraud?

options.A: Authorization of overtime.
options.B: Collection and retention of unclaimed paychecks.
options.C: Distribution of paychecks.
options.D: Authorization of additions and deletions from the payroll.

question: If employee paychecks are distributed by hand to employees, which one of the following departments should be responsible for the safekeeping of unclaimed paychecks?

options.A: Cashier department.
options.B: Timekeeping department.
options.C: Payroll department.
options.D: Production department in which the employee works or worked.

question: Segregation of duties is a fundamental concept in an effective system of internal control. Nevertheless, the internal auditor must be aware that this safeguard can be compromised through

options.A: Lack of training of employees.
options.B: Collusion among employees.
options.C: Absence of internal auditing.
options.D: Irregular employee reviews.

question: Which of the following is most likely to be performed in the control activities component of internal control?

options.A: Assessing fraud risks.
options.B: Ongoing evaluations.
options.C: Risk identification.
options.D: Segregation of duties.

question: Which one of the following situations represents an internal control weakness in accounts receivable?

options.A: Internal auditors confirm customer accounts periodically.
options.B: Customers’ statements are mailed monthly by the accounts receivable department.
options.C: The cashier is denied access to customers’ records and monthly statements.
options.D: Delinquent accounts are reviewed only by the sales manager.

context: Fact Pattern (see image): Randy and John had known each other for many years. They had become best friends in college, where they both majored in accounting. After graduation, Randy took over the family business from his father. His family had been in the grocery business for several generations. When John had difficulty finding a job, Randy offered him a job in the family store. John proved to be a very capable employee. As John demonstrated his abilities, Randy began delegating more and more responsibility to him. After a period of time, John was doing all of the general accounting and authorization functions for checks, cash, inventories, documents, records, and bank reconciliations. (1) John was trusted completely and handled all financial functions. No one checked his work. Randy decided to expand the business and opened several new stores. (2) Randy was always handling the most urgent problem ... “crisis management” is what his college professors had termed it. John assisted with the problems when his other duties allowed him time. Although successful at work, John had (3) difficulties with personal financial problems. At first, the amounts stolen by John were small. John didn't't even worry about making the accounts balance. But John became greedy. “How easy it is to take the money,” he said. He felt that he was a critical member of the business team (4) and that he contributed much more to the success of the company than was represented by his salary. “It would take two or three people to replace me,” he often thought to himself. As the amounts became larger and larger, (5) he made the books balance. Because of these activities, John was able to purchase an expensive car and take his family on several trips each year. (6) He also joined an expensive country club. Things were changing at home, however. (7) John's family observed that he was often argumentative and at other times very depressed. The fraud continued for 6 years. Each year, the business performed more and more poorly. In the last year, the stores had a substantial net loss. Randy's bank required an audit. John confessed when he thought the auditors had discovered his embezzlements. When discussing frauds, the pressures, opportunities, and rationalizations that cause/allow a perpetrator to commit the fraud are often identified. Symptoms of fraud are also studied.
question: Number 1, “John was trusted completely . . .,” is an example of a(n)

options.A: Opportunity to commit.
options.B: Document symptom.
options.C: Lifestyle symptom.
options.D: Situational pressure.

question: Which of the following is the best description of embezzlement?

options.A: Manipulating accounting records to reverse asset impairments.
options.B: Recording fictitious sales in order to receive a higher bonus.
options.C: Shoplifting at a large retail chain where a family member works.
options.D: Employees diverting company funds for personal use.

question: When none of the three fraud risk factors are present, an internal auditor

context: Fact Pattern: Management discovers that a supervisor at one of its restaurant locations removes excess cash and resets sales totals throughout the day on the point-of-sale (POS) system. At closing, the supervisor deposits cash equal to the recorded sales on the POS system and keeps the rest. The supervisor forwards the close-of-day POS reports from the POS system along with a copy of the bank deposit slip to the company’s revenue accounting department. The revenue accounting department records the sales and the cash for the location in the general ledger and verifies the deposit slip to the bank statement. Any differences between sales and deposits are recorded in an over/short account and, if necessary, followed up with the location supervisor. The customer food order checks are serially numbered, and it is the supervisor's responsibility to see that they are accounted for at the end of each day. Customer checks and the transaction journal tapes from the POS system are kept by the supervisor for 1 week at the location and then destroyed.
