context: Fact Pattern (see image): Randy and John had known each other for many years. They had become best friends in college, where they both majored in accounting. After graduation, Randy took over the family business from his father. His family had been in the grocery business for several generations. When John had difficulty finding a job, Randy offered him a job in the family store. John proved to be a very capable employee. As John demonstrated his abilities, Randy began delegating more and more responsibility to him. After a period of time, John was doing all of the general accounting and authorization functions for checks, cash, inventories, documents, records, and bank reconciliations. (1) John was trusted completely and handled all financial functions. No one checked his work. Randy decided to expand the business and opened several new stores. (2) Randy was always handling the most urgent problem ... “crisis management” is what his college professors had termed it. John assisted with the problems when his other duties allowed him time. Although successful at work, John had (3) difficulties with personal financial problems. At first, the amounts stolen by John were small. John didn't't even worry about making the accounts balance. But John became greedy. “How easy it is to take the money,” he said. He felt that he was a critical member of the business team (4) and that he contributed much more to the success of the company than was represented by his salary. “It would take two or three people to replace me,” he often thought to himself. As the amounts became larger and larger, (5) he made the books balance. Because of these activities, John was able to purchase an expensive car and take his family on several trips each year. (6) He also joined an expensive country club. Things were changing at home, however. (7) John's family observed that he was often argumentative and at other times very depressed. The fraud continued for 6 years. Each year, the business performed more and more poorly. In the last year, the stores had a substantial net loss. Randy's bank required an audit. John confessed when he thought the auditors had discovered his embezzlements. context: Fact Pattern: A purchasing agent acquired items for personal use with the organization's funds. The organization allowed designated employees to purchase a specified amount per day in merchandise under open-ended contracts. Supervisory approval of the purchases was required, but that information was not communicated to the vendor. Instead of reviewing and authorizing each purchase order, supervisors routinely signed the authorization sheet at the end of the month without reviewing any of the supporting documentation. Because purchases of this nature were not subject to normal receiving policies, the dishonest employee picked up the supplies at the vendor's warehouse. All purchases were for items routinely ordered by the organization. During the past year, the employee amassed enough merchandise to start a printing and photography business.
question: Which of the following engagement procedures, performed by the internal auditor, is most likely to detect this fraud?

options.A: Recomputing the clerical accuracy of selected vendors’ invoices, including discounts and sales taxes.
options.B: Tracing prices and quantities on selected vendors’ invoices to the related purchase orders.
options.C: Performing a trend analysis of printing supplies expenses for a 2-year period.
options.D: Tracing selected canceled checks to the cash payments journal and to the related vendors' invoices.

question: The internal audit function's responsibility for preventing fraud is to

options.A: Exercise operating authority over fraud prevention activities.
options.B: Evaluate the system of internal control.
options.C: Establish internal control.
options.D: Maintain internal control.

question: The internal audit function has concluded a fraud investigation that revealed a previously undiscovered materially adverse impact on the financial position and results of operations for 2 years on which financial statements have already been

options.A: The chief audit executive should immediately inform
options.B: Senior management and the board.
options.C: The appropriate governmental or regulatory agency.
options.D: The internal accounting function ultimately responsible for making corrective journal entries.

question: Which of the following must be identified as a potential fraud risk?

options.A: Management override of controls.
options.B: Collusion.
options.C: Improper revenue recognition.
options.D: Falsification of documentation.

question: The risk of the addition of fictitious employees to the payroll by the person performing the payroll processing function is reduced by

options.A: Performing periodic floor checks of employees on the payroll.
options.B: Requiring that payroll additions be approved by the controller.
options.C: Requiring the same employee to perform the monthly payroll bank reconciliation.
options.D: Requiring a reconciliation of hours between time cards and hours paid.

question: Fraudulent use of the organization’s credit cards is minimized by which of the following internal control procedures?

options.A: Subjecting credit card charges to the same expense controls as those used on regular organizational expense forms.
options.B: Establishing an organizational policy on the issuance of credit cards to authorized employees.
options.C: Reviewing the validity of credit card need at executive and operating levels on a periodic basis.
options.D: Reconciling the monthly statement from the credit card issuer with the submitted copies of the cardholder's sales receipts.

question: In an audit engagement of revenue recognition processes, how should an internal auditor assess potential fraud risks requiring special attention?

options.A: By applying standard audit procedures and trend-analysis-related anomalies in revenue.
options.B: By relying only on routine testing of revenue transactions and performing analytical review procedures.
options.C: By relying upon the external auditors to have fully addressed fraud risks and interviewing key operating personnel.
options.D: By examining revenue recording controls, reviewing unusual transactions, and testing for misstatements to gauge fraud exposure.

question: When investigating suspected fraud, what is the primary role of the internal audit function?

options.A: To rely on management inquiries to address fraud incidents and question the suspected perpetrator.
options.B: To assist legal counsel in directly interrogating staff accused of committing fraud.
options.C: To oversee fraud investigations by enforcing corrective actions and recommending internal disciplinary measures.
options.D: To conduct independent investigations by gathering evidence, analyzing data, and reporting findings to management and the board.

question: In fraud investigations, how is the internal audit function expected to maintain independence and objectivity?

options.A: By conducting investigations without bias, ensuring that evidence is independently verified and results are communicated impartially.
options.B: By working in close collaboration with the department under review to expedite a timely resolution.
options.C: By referring the fraud allegation to the external auditors, thereby avoiding direct involvement by internal auditing.
options.D: By relying on management-provided data to complete the investigation.

question: Which of the following information technology (IT) departmental responsibilities should be delegated to separate individuals?

options.A: Data entry and quality assurance.
options.B: Data entry and application programming.
options.C: They should never be able to access the code underlying application programs.
options.D: Network maintenance and wireless access.

question: An auditor uncovers a plan to overstate inventory and thereby increase reported profits for a division. The auditor has substantial evidence that the divisional manager was aware of and approved the plan to overstate inventory. There is also some evidence that the manager may have been responsible for the implementation of the plan. The auditor should

options.A: Inform senior management and the audit committee of the findings and discuss possible further investigation.
options.B: Document the case thoroughly and report the suspicions to the external auditor for further review.
options.C: Continue to conduct interviews with subordinates until a definite case is made and then report the case to the audit committee.
options.D: Inform the divisional manager of the auditor's suspicions and obtain the manager's explanation of the findings before pursuing the matter further.

question: What is the role of the internal audit function in a fraud investigation?

options.A: It coordinates with external agencies to evaluate evidence and assist the authorities.
options.B: It relies on reports prepared by the affected departments to compile evidence and questioning staff suspected of wrongdoing.
options.C: It independently collects, analyzes, and verifies evidence related to fraud, ensuring that the investigation remains objective.
options.D: It gathers evidence based on historical data and assists the legal department by interviewing those suspected of fraud.

question: For control purposes, which of the following should be organizationally segregated from the computer operations function?

options.A: Minor maintenance according to a schedule.
options.B: Systems development.
options.C: Data conversion.
options.D: Surveillance of screen display messages.

question: Which of the following controls most likely could prevent personnel from modifying programs to bypass programmed controls?

options.A: Physical security of server rooms to limit access to server equipment.
options.B: Periodic management review of computer utilization reports and systems documentation.
options.C: Segregation of duties for computer programming and computer operations.
options.D: Participation of user department personnel in designing and approving new systems.

question: Questions used to interrogate individuals suspected of fraud should

options.A: Direct the individual to a desired answer.
options.B: Move from the general to the specific.
options.C: Adhere to a predetermined order.
options.D: Cover more than one subject or topic.

context: Fact Pattern: During an engagement performed at a smaller division, the internal auditor notes the following regarding the purchasing function: (1) There are three purchasing agents. Agent 1 is responsible for ordering all large component parts, agent 2 for electric motors, and agent 3 for smaller parts such as fasteners. (2) There are separate accounts payable and receiving departments. (3) In order to hold vendors more responsible, all invoices are sent to the purchasing agent placing the order. The purchasing agent matches the vendor invoice, receiving slip, and purchase order. If all match, the purchasing agent sends the documents forward to the accounts payable department. Differences are investigated by the purchasing agent. (4) Only the accounts payable department has the ability to authorize an item for payment. (5) All recorded receipts are immediately recorded into a perpetual inventory record by the department to which the goods are transferred after receipt. The internal auditor interviewed both management and the purchasing agents. Both groups were very satisfied with the current system because it helps maintain vendor accountability and provides sufficient segregation of duties given that only the accounts payable department can authorize an item for payment.
question: Which of the following controls, if properly implemented, is most likely to decrease the likelihood of fraud?

options.A: Require periodic rotation of purchases among different vendors.
options.B: Require that receiving reports be sent directly to accounts payable.
options.C: Require rotation of duties among the three purchasing agents.
options.D: Require that the updates to the perpetual inventory record be made by the receiving department.

question: A significant employee fraud took place shortly after an internal auditing engagement. The internal auditor may not have properly fulfilled the responsibility for the prevention of fraud by failing to note and report that

options.A: There were no written policies describing prohibited activities and the action required whenever violations are discovered.
options.B: Divisional employees had not been properly trained to distinguish between bona fide signatures and cleverly forged ones on authorization forms.
options.C: A system of control that depended upon separation of duties could be circumvented by collusion among three employees.
options.D: Policies, practices, and procedures to monitor activities and safeguard assets were less extensive in low-risk areas than in high-risk areas.

question: Internal auditors have a responsibility for helping to deter fraud. Which of the following best describes how this responsibility is usually met?

options.A: By testing for fraud in every engagement and following up as appropriate.
options.B: By assisting in the design of control systems to prevent fraud.
options.C: By coordinating with security personnel and law enforcement agencies in the investigation of possible frauds.
options.D: By evaluating the adequacy and effectiveness of controls in light of the potential exposure or risk.

question: An internal auditor discovers facts suggesting that a vice president has committed unethical acts. The internal auditor should

options.A: Confront the vice president with the facts before proceeding.
options.B: Conduct an investigation to determine the extent of the vice president's involvement in the unethical acts.
options.C: Report the facts to the chief executive officer and the audit committee.
options.D: Schedule an audit of the business function involved.

question: A payroll clerk working through a computerized payroll system increased the hourly pay rate of two employees and shared the resulting overpayments with the employees. Which of the following would have best served to prevent this illegal act?

options.A: Requiring that all changes to pay records be recorded on a standard form.
options.B: Monitoring of payroll costs by department heads on a monthly basis.
options.C: Reconciling pay rates per personnel records with those of the payroll system annually.
options.D: Limiting access to master payroll records to supervisory personnel in the payroll department.

question: An auditor is concerned with controls designed to safeguard assets that are relevant to the reliability of financial reporting. Adequate safeguards over access to and use of assets means protection from

options.A: Losses such as those arising from setting a product price too low and subsequently realizing operating losses from the product's sale.
options.B: Losses arising from access by unauthorized persons.
options.C: Only those losses arising from fraud.
options.D: Any management decision that would unprofitably use company resources.

question: Which of the following is an example of management override?

options.A: Posting adjusting entries after year-end analyses have indicated changes in the overall economic environment.
options.B: Changing accounting estimates in response to a recommendation by the external auditor.
options.C: Extending payment periods for certain vendors beyond those allowed by company policy.
options.D: Changing accounts payable procedures in response to a recommendation by the internal auditor.

question: When interviewing an individual suspected of fraud, the interviewer should

options.A: Pay attention to the wording choices of the suspect.
options.B: Ensure the suspect's supervisor is present during the interview.
options.C: Lock the door to ensure no one will interrupt the interview.
options.D: Ask if the suspect committed the fraud.

question: How can an internal auditor use interviewing techniques to support fraud investigations while upholding objectivity?

options.A: By adopting a structured approach that combines open-ended questions, thorough documentation, and independent verification of responses.
options.B: By focusing on confirming management's suspicions to provide an efficient and effective interview.
options.C: By adhering to a rigid script that limits the opportunity for the conversation to go off course.
options.D: By allowing the conversation to flow informally without a structured interview plan, relying on spontaneity.

question: How does the internal audit function ensure the integrity of fraud investigations?

options.A: By conducting reviews that focus primarily on compliance and interviewing staff suspected of fraud.
options.B: By performing thorough, unbiased reviews of fraud claims and validating evidence before reporting findings to the appropriate oversight bodies.
options.C: By outsourcing the evidence validation process entirely to third-party specialists, eliminating the need for oversight.
options.D: By accepting initial fraud reports and relying on management's review of the incident.

context: Fact Pattern: A fraud was perpetrated in a moderate-sized organization when the accounting clerk was delegated too much responsibility. During the year, the organization switched suppliers of a service to a new vendor. The accounting clerk continued to submit fraudulent invoices from the “old supplier.” Because contracting for services and approval of supplier invoices had been delegated to the clerk, it was possible for the clerk to continue billings from the old supplier and deposit the subsequent checks, which the clerk was responsible to mail, into a new account the clerk opened in the name of the old supplier. The clerk was considered an excellent employee and eventually was improperly given the added responsibility of preparing the department budgets. This added responsibility allowed the clerk to budget for the amount of the fraudulent payments.
question: Which of the following controls would have been least likely to prevent or detect the fraud described?

options.A: Mailing of checks by someone other than the person responsible for check signing or invoice approval.
options.B: Comparison by the person signing checks of invoices with an independent verification of services received.
options.C: Budget preparation by someone other than the person signing contracts and approving payment.
options.D: Requiring authorization of payments by someone other than the clerk negotiating the contract.

question: A means of ensuring that payroll checks are drawn for properly authorized amounts is to

options.A: Witness the distribution of payroll checks.
options.B: Conduct periodic floor verification of employees on the payroll.
options.C: Require that undelivered checks be returned to the cashier.
options.D: Require supervisory approval of employee time cards.

question: How can internal auditors best evaluate the impact of the tone at the top on fraud risk within an organization?

options.A: By reviewing external audit results and communications and testing of financial controls.
options.B: By assessing how senior management's ethical behavior and communication practices influence the design and execution of fraud prevention controls.
options.C: By focusing on the internal control assessments and testing cash receipts and disbursements.
options.D: By measuring the quantitative outcomes of previous fraud incidents and evaluating internal controls over cash receipts and disbursements.

question: Which of the following statements is (are) true regarding the prevention of fraud?

options.A: Only management is responsible for the prevention and detection of fraud.
options.B: Internal auditors implement the controls designed to prevent and detect fraud.
options.C: Effective internal controls can eliminate the probability of fraud.
options.D: The primary means of preventing fraud is through internal control established and maintained by management.

question: Internal auditors and management have become increasingly concerned about computer fraud. Which of the following control procedures is least important in preventing computer fraud?

options.A: Segregation of duties between the programmer and systems analyst.
options.B: Segregation of duties between the applications programmer and the program librarian function.
options.C: Testing of new applications by users during the systems development process.
options.D: Program change control requiring a distinction between production programs and test programs.

question: The manager of a production line has the authority to order and receive replacement parts for all machinery that requires periodic maintenance. The internal auditor received an anonymous tip that the manager ordered substantially more parts than were necessary from a family member in the parts supply business. The unneeded parts were never delivered. Instead, the manager processed receiving documents and charged the parts to machinery maintenance accounts. The payments for the undelivered parts were sent to the supplier, and the money was divided between the manager and the family member. Which of the following internal controls would have most likely prevented this fraud from occurring?

options.A: Using the company’s inventory system to match quantities requested with quantities received.
options.B: Establishing predefined spending levels for all vendors during the bidding process.
options.C: Comparing the bill of lading for replacement parts to the approved purchase order.
options.D: Segregating the receiving function from the authorization of parts purchases.

question: How does fraud awareness training support fraud prevention?

options.A: Reduces opportunities to commit fraud.
options.B: Helps develop credible responses to potential risks.
options.C: Limits rationalization.
options.D: Facilitates the testing of controls.

question: Which of the following gives the internal auditor the authority to investigate fraud?

options.A: The internal audit mandate.
options.B: Common law.
options.C: The Glo
options.D: Management.

question: An internal auditor identifies a potential conflict of interest involving an employee. What should the internal auditor do?

options.A: Recommend terminating the employee to management.
options.B: Investigate further by gathering additional information and evidence regarding the relationship between the employee and the vendor.
options.C: Immediately notify law enforcement authorities about the conflict of interest.
options.D: Conclude that no fraud has occurred because no evidence of financial loss exists.

question: During a fraud investigation, which interviewing technique best encourages witnesses to provide detailed, candid responses?

options.A: Using leading questions that suggest a desired response to guide the interviewee.
options.B: By following an organized script of standard questions that often prove effective.
options.C: Asking yes-or-no questions to get the perpetrator to admit wrongdoing.
options.D: Asking open-ended questions that invite narrative responses and elaboration.

question: After completing an investigation, internal auditing has concluded that an employee has stolen a significant amount of cash receipts. A draft of the proposed communication on this observation should be submitted for review to

options.A: A Legal counsel.
options.B: The organization's outside auditors.
options.C: The board.
options.D: The chief executive officer of the organization.

question: In the organization of the information systems function, the most important segregation of duties is

options.A: Not allowing the data librarian to assist in data processing operations.
options.B: Using different programming personnel to maintain utility programs from those who maintain the application programs.
options.C: Assuring that those responsible for programming the system do not have access to data processing operations.
options.D: Having a separate information officer at the top level of the organization outside of the accounting function.

question: A programmer’s accumulation of roundoff errors into one account, which is later accessed by the programmer, is a type of computer fraud. The best way to prevent this type of fraud is to

options.A: Independently test programs during development and limit access to the programs.
options.B: Use control totals and check the results of the computer.
options.C: Segregate duties of systems development and programming.
options.D: Build in judgment with reasonableness tests.

question: Which of the following describes one of the responsibilities of the internal auditor for the deterrence of fraud in an organization?

options.A: Prosecuting perpetrators of fraud.
options.B: Implementation of systems to discourage fraud.
options.C: Reporting suspected fraud to law enforcement personnel.
options.D: Evaluating the adequacy of controls to prevent fraud.

question: Which of the following statement(s) is (are) true regarding the role of internal auditors in the deterrence of fraud?

options.A: Internal auditors are responsible for assisting in the deterrence of fraud by examining and evaluating the adequacy of controls.
options.B: Internal auditors are responsible for designing and implementing fraud prevention controls.
options.C: Internal auditors design and implement communication channels that provide management with information on the reliability of controls.
options.D: Internal auditors set the appropriate tone at the top and the appetite for fraud risk.

question: How does the principle of segregation of duties best serve as an effective control to prevent and detect fraudulent activities?

options.A: By centralizing responsibilities to increase administrative efficiency and relying on periodic external reviews for fraud detection.
options.B: By automating processes to the extent that human intervention is minimized and conducting annual internal audit engagements.
options.C: By placing similar tasks within the same department and having the accounting department provide routine transaction monitoring.
options.D: By designing controls so that no individual is responsible for all aspects of a transaction, ensuring independent verification at each step.

question: A chief audit executive (CAE) suspects that several employees have used desktop computers for personal gain. In conducting an investigation, the primary reason that the CAE chose to engage a forensic information systems auditor rather than using the organization's information systems auditor is that a forensic information systems auditor would possess

options.A: Knowledge of the computing system that would enable a more comprehensive assessment of the computer use and abuse.
options.B: Superior documentation and organization skills that would facilitate in the presentation of findings to senior management and the board.
options.C: Knowledge of what constitutes evidence acceptable in a court of law. >
options.D: Superior analytical skills that would facilitate the identification of computer abuse.

question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding audit engagement workpaper documentation for a fraud investigation?

options.A: Incriminating evidence and important testimonial evidence should be documented, but interview transcripts should not be documented because they are confidential.
options.B: Only incriminating evidence should be documented.
options.C: Only testimonial evidence should be documented.
options.D: Incriminating evidence, important testimonial evidence, and transcripts of interviews with suspected perpetrators should be documented.

question: Internal auditors assist in fraud prevention by evaluating controls. An internal auditor is most likely to conclude that which segregation of duties is unnecessary?

options.A: Negotiating a contract and approving payments.
options.B: Ordering goods and receiving the goods.
options.C: Preparing a sales order and approving extension of credit to the customer.
options.D: Approving an electronic payment and verifying receipt of a good or service.

question: How does senior management's tone at the top affect individual engagement risks related to fraud?

options.A: It helps ensure the effectiveness of the system of internal controls.
options.B: It influences employee behavior by promoting ethical conduct and reducing opportunities for fraudulent activities in day-to-day operations.
options.C: It emphasizes strategic decision making and the monitoring of operational budgets.
options.D: It primarily impacts financial reporting misstatement risk and budget monitoring.

question: Which of the following is the most effective detective control to identify fraudulent disbursements in an organization's accounts payable process?

options.A: Requiring dual approval for all vendor payment requests.
options.B: Reconciling the accounts payable subsidiary ledger to the general ledger on a monthly basis.
options.C: Segregating the duties of invoice processing and payment approval.
options.D: Restricting access to blank check stock to authorized personnel only.

question: During an engagement involving the purchasing department, an internal auditor learned that one vendor rewarded buyers in proportion to the size of the orders received. What recommendation should the internal auditor make to reduce the likelihood of future acceptance of such rewards by the buyers?

options.A: Periodic review of buyer lifestyles.
options.B: A strong, written statement of management's commitment to organizational ethics.
options.C: A policy of identifying and reducing buyer situational pressures.
options.D: Establishing an employee counseling program.

question: If an internal auditor is interviewing three individuals, one of whom is suspected of committing a fraud, which of the following is the least effective approach?

options.A: Ask each individual to prepare a written statement explaining the individual's actions.
options.B: Attempt to get the suspected individual to confess.
options.C: Listen carefully to what each interviewee has to say.
options.D: Take the role of one seeking the truth.

question: In evaluating risk controls, how can the implementation of defined authority levels reduce the likelihood of fraud?

options.A: By providing full authority to appropriate operating management along with routine internal auditing.
options.B: By allowing flexible role assignments that adapt quickly to changing business needs with ongoing transaction monitoring.
options.C: By establishing distinct roles with clear limits on decision-making power, thereby ensuring that each critical function is independently verified.
options.D: By centralizing decision-making authority with top management to maintain consistency and reduce administrative overhead.

question: Which of the following is a responsibility of internal auditors regarding fraud prevention, deterrence, and detection?

options.A: Prepare the annual disclosure of whether the organization has a code of ethics that covers its chief executive officer (CEO) and senior financial officers.
options.B: Raise fraud awareness within the organization, including encouraging the audit committee and senior management to set the proper “tone at the top.”
options.C: Develop an approach the organization can use to sustain antibribery principles in every country in which the organization operates.
options.D: Implement an effective system of internal controls.

question: Proper segregation of duties reduces the opportunities to allow persons to be in positions both to

options.A: Establish internal control and authorize transactions.
options.B: Record cash receipts and cash disbursements.
options.C: Journalize entries and prepare financial statements.
options.D: Perpetrate and conceal fraud and error.

question: In asmall public company that has few levels of management with wide spans of control, which of the following mitigates management override of controls?

options.A: An authoritarian CEO who has imposed strict penalties for unethical behavior.
options.B: Having two officers who significantly influence management and operations.
options.C: Establishing a corporate culture in which integrity and ethical values are highly appreciated.
options.D: A generous performance-based reward system.

question: An internal auditor's fraud risk assessment is most likely to determine that which of the following is an inappropriate practice in the purchase function?

options.A: An accounts payable authorized signature list is prepared.
options.B: A policy prohibits receipt of gifts from vendors.
options.C: Purchases are made only from approved vendors.
options.D: The receiving department uses an approved order for goods stating the amount ordered.

question: How can internal auditors verify the reliability of information obtained during fraud investigation interviews?

options.A: By relying on the interview transcript to avoid the need for additional investigation.
options.B: By cross-checking responses with independent evidence and corroborating statements with additional data sources.
options.C: By using standardized questions that have proven effective in prior investigations.
options.D: By accepting interview responses to the extent that they align with the auditors’ expectations.
